import (

type initFlags struct {
	domain          string
	system          string
	envs            []string
	templateVersion string
	values          []string
	sets            []string
	noInput         bool
	plan            bool
	force           bool

}

var initFlagValues = initFlags{output: deploy.OutputPlain}

var deployInitCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "init [component...]",
	Short: "Scaffold a system's manifests into the GitOps repository",
	Long: "Generate the kustomize tree a system needs in the GitOps repository, from the topology its host " +
		"declares.\n\n" +
		"Onboarding a component is otherwise entirely manual: somebody hand-writes component.yaml, base/ and an " +
		"overlay per environment, for every block, in every customer repository. This does that, and fills in " +
		"every fact the CLI can derive — the block's workload, the app-ids that belong in a Dapr component's " +
		"scopes, the environments deploy.yaml defines, the registry.\n\n" +
		"Complete manifests are not the goal. Connection strings, hosts, credentials and cron schedules cannot be " +
		"derived, so they are emitted as REPLACE-ME-<HINT> placeholders and reported as a list when the run " +
		"finishes. Filling those in is the developer's remaining job. Image tags are not in that list: " +
		"`intropy deploy` pins digests, and scaffolding must never pin one.\n\n" +
		"The system's shared objects — the Dapr pub/sub and secret store its blocks resolve by name, and the " +
		"secrets behind them — go in a `host` directory of their own. A Dapr Component is namespace-scoped and " +
		"every integration in the namespace shares it, so exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one; the " +
		"host directory is what gives them that owner, and scopes: is what limits who may use them.\n\n" +
		"--domain places the system in the tree. Note this differs from every other deploy subcommand, where " +
		"--domain narrows a search: here it is a destination. You rarely need it: the domain comes from where " +
		"the system already sits in the GitOps tree, and failing that from the workspace's own " +
		"domains/<domain>/<system>/ layout, which every integrations tree mirrors from the deployment tree. " +
		"Pass it explicitly to place a system somewhere else, or when the workspace has another shape.\n\n" +
		"A workspace holding several systems needs --system to say which one. It is matched against each " +
		"scaffolded host's recorded system name and its system directory, both of which are on disk, so " +
		"picking a system never builds the others.\n\n" +
		"The manifests come from the template library's latest release; --template-version renders from a specific tag " +
		"instead, which is what makes a re-run reproducible while the templates are still moving.\n\n" +
		"Nothing is pushed to the default branch: a tree full of placeholders would be picked up by the " +
		"ApplicationSet immediately. The run pushes deploy-init/<domain>-<system> for review instead. Re-running " +
		"is additive and safe — a file that already exists and differs is reported and left alone unless --force " +
		"is given, and --force still refuses to overwrite an overlay that pins a digest.\n\n" +
		"With --plan nothing is written and git is not touched at all.",
	Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
		if err := validateOutputFlag(initFlagValues.output, deploy.OutputPlain, deploy.OutputJSON); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		sets, err := template.ParseSets(initFlagValues.sets)
		if err != nil {
			return newUsageErrorf("%v", err)
		}

		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()

		return deploy.Init(ctx, deploy.InitOptions{
			Components:      args,
			Domain:          initFlagValues.domain,
			System:          initFlagValues.system,
			Environments:    initFlagValues.envs,
			TemplateVersion: initFlagValues.templateVersion,
			Files:           initFlagValues.values,
			SetValues:       sets,
			NoInput:         initFlagValues.noInput,
			PlanOnly:        initFlagValues.plan,
			Force:           initFlagValues.force,
			GitopsRepo:      initFlagValues.gitopsRepo,
			OutputFormat:    initFlagValues.output,
			Color:           useColor(cmd),
			UserAgent:       "intropy-cli/" + version,
			CliVersion:      version,
			Stdin:           cmd.InOrStdin(),
			Stdout:          cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:          cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
		})
	},
}

func init() {
	f := deployInitCmd.Flags()
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.domain, "domain", "", "domain to place the system under (default: where it already is in the GitOps tree, else the workspace's domains/<domain>/ layout)")
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.system, "system", "", "system to scaffold; selects the host when the workspace holds several (default: the only one)")
	f.StringArrayVar(&initFlagValues.envs, "environments", nil, "environments to create overlays for (repeatable; default: every environment in deploy.yaml)")
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.templateVersion, "template-version", "", "template release tag (default: latest)")
	f.StringArrayVarP(&initFlagValues.values, "values", "f", nil, "values file (repeatable; - reads one document from stdin)")
	f.StringArrayVarP(&initFlagValues.sets, "set", "s", nil, "set a template value as key=value (repeatable)")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.noInput, "no-input", false, "never prompt; fail if a required value is missing")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.plan, "plan", false, "report what would be written without writing it or touching git")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.force, "force", false, "overwrite files that already differ (refused for an overlay that pins a digest)")
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.gitopsRepo, "gitops-repo", "", "GitOps repository URL (default: gitopsRepo from config, or INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO)")
	f.StringVarP(&initFlagValues.output, "output", "o", deploy.OutputPlain, "output format (plain, json)")

	deployCmd.AddCommand(deployInitCmd)
}

---

# Code Comment Analysis — intropy-cli

Overall the codebase is in **very good shape** on the criteria you set. The dominant comment voice is exactly what you want: explain *why* the code does what it does and what invariants a human needs to hold, not *what* changed. I found **no change-history comments** ("fixed X", "used to do Y", "now instead of Z") and **no TODO/FIXME/HACK debt markers**. The problems are concentrated in two areas: **(1) a long tail of exported types and cobra commands with no documentation at all**, and (2) a handful of doc comments that tip from "thorough" into "bloated."

## Verdict by criterion

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Comments explain what/why, not "what changed" | ✅ Clean — no change-history found |
| Not overly bloated | ⚠️ Mostly good; ~6 doc blocks are 12–16 lines and could be tightened |
| Comments on all important parts | ❌ Uneven — `internal/` is well-served, `cmd/intropy` and parts of `internal/skill`, `internal/registry`, `internal/skill/oci` are not |

---

## 1. Coverage gaps (the main issue)

Comment density by directory (non-test files):

```
internal/git:        32%   internal/topology:   31%   internal/config:     31%
internal/source:     26%   internal/gitops:     25%   internal/dashboard:  24%
internal/command:    24%   internal/deploy:     22%   internal/release:    19%
internal/argocd:     19%   internal/kustomize:  18%   internal/template:   14%
internal/system:     14%   internal/registry:    8%   internal/skill:       7%
internal/skill/oci:   5%   cmd/intropy:          2%
```

### `cmd/intropy` — 2% comment density

Most cobra commands are entirely uncommented. The `Long:` help text does carry the user-facing documentation load, so this is partially defensible — but there is no developer-facing documentation for the command wiring itself. Files with zero comments and nontrivial logic:

- `skills_update.go` (121 lines) — reconciliation loop, signal handling, output formatting
- `skills_collection_update.go` (121 lines)
- `skills_publish.go` (112 lines)
- `deploy_init.go` (112 lines) — note: `deploy_init.go` has an *excellent* `Long:` description (10 paragraphs), but the `RunE` body and flag struct are uncommented
- `deploy_sync.go`, `deploy_diff.go`, `release_create.go`, `sys_create.go`, `dashboard.go`, `int_list.go`, `int_describe.go`, `release_view.go`, `release_list.go`

`deploy_init.go` is actually the *right* pattern (rich `Long:` text) — but the rest of the commands don't follow it. They get one-or-two-sentence `Long:` strings and nothing else.

### `internal/skill` and `internal/skill/oci` — 5–7%

Exported types and constructors with no doc comments:

- `skill.Project`, `skill.NewUpdater`, `skill.NewInstaller`, `skill.NewAdder`, `skill.NewCollectionInstaller`, `skill.NewCollectionPublisher`
- `skill.Updater` struct, `skill.Installer` struct (only methods are documented)
- `skill.Manifest`, `skill.ManifestCollection`, `skill.LockSource`
- `skill.LoadLockfile`, `skill.SaveLockfile`, `skill.NewTarGzExtractor`
- `oci.Artifact`, `oci.Index`, `oci.IndexEntry`, `oci.NewClient`, `oci.ParseReference`
- `oci.Client.Pull` — has zero comments, despite being the package's main entry point and doing non-trivial validation (`ErrNotSkill` checks on artifactType, layer count, media type)

### `internal/registry` — 8%

- `registry.Descriptor`, `registry.Artifact`, `registry.Index`, `registry.Client`, `registry.Option`, `registry.NewClient`, `registry.ParseReference` — all undocumented exported symbols.
- `registry/push.go` has only a 2-line comment on `PushArtifact` for 86 lines of OCI manifest assembly — a non-trivial function.

---

## 2. Bloated comments (minor issue)

The house style leans toward long, discursive doc comments. Most earn their length by explaining invariants and trade-offs, but a few tip over:

**`internal/deploy/safepath.go:13–28`** (16 lines) — explains the `destTree` symlink policy. Good content, but the two-bullet justification could lose 4–5 lines without losing meaning.

**`internal/deploy/diff.go:17–31`** (15 lines on `Diff`) — the *contrast* with `--plan` is useful, but the third paragraph (about ArgoCD doing the rendering) restates what the code makes obvious.

**`internal/deploy/plan.go:273–285`** (13 lines on `assertPinsRendered`) — the explanation of why matching the full `image@digest` is essential is valuable; the second paragraph about `newName` is the part that strains.

**`internal/config/config.go:1–13`** (13-line package doc) — fine content, but the precedence rules (`flag > env > file > zero`) are also documented at the field level, so this is duplicated.

**`internal/deploy/scaffold.go:79–90`, `promote.go:175–187`, `init.go:509–519`** — similar pattern: the "why" is real but the phrasing is doing 1.5× the work it needs to.

This is a matter of taste, not correctness. The tone is consistent and purposeful — I'd call these "could be tighter," not "bloated" in the pejorative sense.

---

## 3. What the codebase does well (keep doing)

- **Invariant-focused comments.** `internal/deploy/plan.go`'s `applyEdits` and `assertPinsRendered` explain *why* a stale release annotation must be removed, and *why* matching the full `image@digest` matters. These are exactly the comments a future maintainer needs.
- **"Deliberately not" comments.** `internal/gitops/remote.go:15` ("*Deliberately not used to derive the cache directory…*") and `internal/config/config.go:31` ("*Borrowed, not ours — do not rename them*") — these prevent well-intentioned refactors from breaking things.
- **Error-message rationale.** `internal/deploy/diff.go:127` ("*…an unlabelled failure leaves nobody able to tell which*") explains why an error is phrased a certain way.
- **No debt markers.** Zero TODOs, FIXMEs, HACKs in non-test code.

---

## Recommendations (priority order)

1. **Add doc comments to exported symbols in `internal/skill`, `internal/skill/oci`, `internal/registry`.** This is the biggest gap. Constructors (`NewX`), struct types, and the main entry points (`oci.Client.Pull`, `registry.Client.PushArtifact`) all deserve at least one sentence. Run `golint`/`staticcheck` with the `ST1000`/`ST1020`/`ST1021`/`ST1022` style checks to catch these mechanically.

2. **Lift the `cmd/intropy` commands to the standard of `deploy_init.go`.** Either expand `Long:` for the thin commands, or add a brief package-level comment per command file explaining the flow. Right now a maintainer has to reverse-engineer the relationship between `skills_update.go` and `skill.Updater`.

3. **Tighten the ~6 longest doc blocks** listed above. Target ≤ 10 lines each. Cut the second-order justification paragraphs; keep the invariant and the consequence.

4. **Add a CI check** (`go vet` with a custom analyzer, or `golangci-lint` with `godot`/`godox`/`dupl` and the revive `exported` rule) so undocumented exported symbols and stale comment styles fail the build rather than accumulating.

The good news: there is **no change-history cleanup** needed. The work is almost entirely additive — filling in coverage gaps — plus a light trim pass on a handful of long doc blocks.

I have a complete picture. Here's the extended analysis.

---

# CLI Documentation & Output Text Analysis

## A. CLI help text (`Long:` descriptions)

### The core tension: house style is "essay," not "reference"

The deploy/release command group treats `--help` as a long-form explanation of *philosophy and invariants*. This is defensible for a GitOps tool where the conceptual model is non-obvious — but it makes the help genuinely hard to scan.

| Command | Words | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `deploy init` | **473** | Bloated — 10 paragraphs of mixed concerns |
| `deploy status` | **253** | Bloated — explains the *philosophy* of consistency, not the table |
| `deploy pin` | **229** | Long but mostly load-bearing |
| `deploy promote` | **203** | Long but mostly load-bearing |
| `deploy diff` | **198** | Mostly good; the "not deploy --plan" paragraph is essential disambiguation |
| `release create` | **173** | Fine |
| `deploy sync` | **169** | Fine — the "reviewed-revision guard" is non-obvious |
| `skills collection update` | 85 | Good — concrete `--ref` vs no-`--ref` distinction |
| `skills add` | 82 | Good |
| `skills update` | 75 | Good |

**The bloated ones share a pattern:** they explain *why the command exists* and *what design decision it embodies*, when what a `--help` reader needs is *what it does*, *what flags it takes*, and *what it costs*.

### Specific examples of bloat

**`deploy init` (473 words)** — this is a wall of text. It covers:
1. What it does (1 sentence, good)
2. Why manual onboarding is painful (justification, not usage)
3. What placeholders are (essential)
4. The architecture of the `host` directory and Dapr Components (concept, not usage)
5. `--domain` semantics (essential — it differs from other subcommands)
6. `--system` semantics (essential)
7. Template versioning (essential)
8. Git branch strategy (essential)
9. `--force` semantics (essential)
10. `--plan` (essential)

Items 2, 4, and the "Complete manifests are not the goal" preamble are philosophy. They belong in `docs/` or `deploy init --explain`, not in `--help`. Cutting them would bring this to ~250 words.

**`deploy status` (253 words)** — the second paragraph ("Promotion copies digests rather than rebuilding, so the same digest in every row is what makes 'production runs the bits staging tested' a fact rather than a hope") is a *justification of GitOps promotion*, not help for `deploy status`. The reader already ran `deploy status`; they've bought in. What they need is: what the columns mean, why a row might be blank, and what "consistent" means.

### Inconsistency: the `skills` group vs the `deploy` group

The two command groups have wildly different documentation voices:

```
deploy group:  long-form, second-person, discursive, "you are reviewing…"
skills group:  terse, imperative, reference-style
```

A user moving between them feels the shift. Neither is wrong; they should pick one.

### Inconsistency: flag descriptions

The *same flag* is described three different ways across commands:

- `--argocd-server`:
  - `deploy diff`: "ArgoCD server to **render through**"
  - `deploy pin`: "ArgoCD server to **watch**"
  - `deploy promote`: "ArgoCD server to **consult**"
  - `deploy status`: "ArgoCD server to **read from**"
  - `deploy sync`: "ArgoCD server to **sync through**"

  The verb drift is technically accurate but reads as noise. Pick one ("ArgoCD server to contact" or just "ArgoCD server address").

- `--env`:
  - `deploy pin`: "target environment"
  - `deploy diff`: "environment to review"
  - `deploy sync`: "environment to apply"

  Same problem.

- `--output`:
  - `"output format (plain, json)"` (most commands)
  - `"output format: 'json' writes the result document to stdout"` (`int create`, `sys create`)
  - `"output format: plain or json"` (`skills add`, `skills list`, `skills update`, `skills collection *`)

  Three distinct styles.

### Inconsistency: `Use:` strings

```
deploy init     → "init [component...]"       (variadic optional)
deploy pin      → "pin <component> [version]" (one required, one optional)
deploy promote  → "promote <component>"       (one required)
deploy sync     → "sync <component>"
deploy diff     → "diff <component>"
deploy status   → "status <component>"
release create  → "create <component>"
release list    → "list <component>"
release view    → "view <component> <version>"
int create      → "create <template>"
int describe    → "describe <template>"
int list        → "list [dir]"
sys create      → "create"                    (no args — but --name is required!)
```

`sys create` is the outlier: `Use: "create"` with no positional args, but `--name` is a required flag. That's a CLI anti-pattern; if `--name` is required it should probably be `create <name>`.

---

## B. Static output text (what users see at runtime)

### The good

- **Consistent progress voice.** `internal/deploy` uses a uniform lowercase, present-tense progress style: `"syncing %s on %s at %s"`, `"reading %s"`, `"pushed %s to %s"`. Easy to scan.
- **Action-oriented next steps.** `deploy diff` ends with `"apply this with:\n  intropy deploy sync %s --env %s --revision %s\n"` — exactly what a confused user needs.
- **Structured empty-states.** `skills list` says `"No skills installed."` and follows with `"Use \`intropy skills add <ref>\` to add one."` — good.
- **The summary sentence under `deploy status`** is a genuine UX win — `"all 3 environments run sha256:abc… — these are the same bits, promoted rather than rebuilt"` is the answer to the question the user asked.

### The hard-to-understand

**`deploy status` — `summarise()` output is dense and grammar-stilted:**

```
the environments do not all run the same bits: staging runs sha256:abc…;
prod runs sha256:def…; qa pins no digest at all
```

The phrasing "do not all run the same bits" is doing a lot of work. "Bits" is GitOps jargon that the rest of the CLI mostly avoids (it says "image digest" elsewhere). Consider: `"environments disagree: staging → sha256:abc…, prod → sha256:def…, qa has no digest pinned"`.

**`deploy status` notes — passive voice:**

```
staging pins ghcr.io/example/api to the tag "v1.2.3" rather than a digest,
so what it runs can change without a deployment
```

Grammatically correct but backwards. The *consequence* should come first: `"staging can drift without a deployment: it pins the tag "v1.2.3" rather than a digest"`.

**`deploy init` placeholder summary:**

```
Image tags are not in this list: intropy deploy pins digests, so leave them alone.
```

This line only makes sense if you already understand the placeholder/digest distinction. It's a clarification for a confusion the user doesn't yet have. Either drop it or move it into the placeholder list header.

### The bloated

**Error messages that explain the *why* inline:**

```
%s's pending change is %s, not %s.
%s has advanced since you reviewed it — read the new diff before syncing
```

The second sentence is right; the first is restating what the user already knows from the error. Could be one line: `"pending change is %s, not the %s you reviewed — re-run 'intropy deploy diff %s --env %s' before syncing"`.

```
--force would overwrite %d overlay%s that pin a digest, un-deploying what they run:
%s

Remove those paths from the scaffold, or delete the overlay deliberately first.
```

"un-deploying what they run" is editorializing. The user already knows what `--force` does or they wouldn't have passed it.

### Inconsistent formatting conventions

| Convention | Where used |
|---|---|
| `verb: object` (lowercase) | `internal/deploy` — `"reading %s"`, `"pushed %s to %s"` |
| `Verb object.` (sentence) | `cmd/intropy` — `"Added %s @ %s"`, `"Published %s"`, `"Registered collection %q"` |
| `Verb object` (no period) | `skills update` — `"Updated %s: %s -> %s"` |

The `internal/deploy` style is the most consistent and the most readable. The `cmd/intropy` sentence-style with capital and period feels out of place in a CLI.

Also: `skills add` and `skills collection add` use `->`, while `skills update` uses `->`, but `int_create_skills.go` uses both `->` *and* `… @ …`. Pick one arrow and stick to it.

---

## C. Recommendations

### High priority

1. **Cut `deploy init`'s `Long:` from 473 → ~200 words.** Move the architecture/philosophy paragraphs (Dapr ownership model, "complete manifests are not the goal") to a `docs/deploy-init.md` or a `--explain` flag. Keep: what it does, the placeholder contract, `--domain`/`--system` semantics, the git branch strategy, `--force`/`--plan`.

2. **Cut `deploy status`'s `Long:` from 253 → ~120 words.** Drop the "why promotion is good" paragraph. Keep: column meanings, why a row can be blank, the meaning of `consistent`, exit-code contract.

3. **Normalize flag descriptions.** Define shared constants:
   ```go
   const (
       flagArgocdServer = "ArgoCD server address (default: argocdServer from config, ARGOCD_SERVER, or deploy.yaml)"
       flagOutputFormat = "output format (plain, json)"
       flagEnv          = "target environment (required)"
   )
   ```
   This kills the verb drift and the three `--output` styles at once.

4. **Fix `sys create`'s `Use:`** — either make `--name` positional (`Use: "create <name>"`) or accept that a required flag is fine but document it: the current state is the worst of both.

### Medium priority

5. **Pick one output voice and enforce it.** The `internal/deploy` style (lowercase, present-tense, no trailing period) is the most consistent and the most scannable. Apply it to `cmd/intropy`'s completion messages (`"Added %s"`, `"Published %s"`, `"Registered collection %q"`).

6. **Rewrite `deploy status`'s `summarise()` for plain language.** Drop "bits" in favor of "image digest" (the term the rest of the CLI uses). Front-load the verdict: `"environments disagree: …"` not `"the environments do not all run the same bits: …"`.

7. **Front-load consequences in notes.** `"staging pins the tag "v1.2.3" rather than a digest — it can drift without a deployment"` is easier to scan than the current `"…so what it runs can change without a deployment"` tail.

### Low priority

8. **Standardize arrows.** `->` everywhere, or `@` everywhere, but not both. `->` is more common in the codebase; keep that.

9. **Consider a shared `--explain` convention.** Several commands would benefit from a "tell me more" mode that prints the philosophy the `Long:` currently carries. That keeps `--help` scannable while preserving the educational content the authors clearly care about.

---

## Summary

The code comments are in better shape than the CLI surface. The help text has a clear house style — discursive, explanatory, second-person — and it's applied well in the `deploy`/`release` groups but unevenly elsewhere. The two genuine bloat cases are `deploy init` (473 words) and `deploy status` (253 words), both of which explain *philosophy* when they should explain *usage*.

The static output text is mostly consistent within `internal/deploy` but drifts at the `cmd/intropy` boundary. The fix is mechanical: shared flag-description constants, a single output voice, and a lighter touch on the two longest `Long:` blocks.

```
│   │   ├── publish <spec-file> <ref>  --force
│   │   └── update <alias>  --ref --output -o
│   ├── list                --output -o
│   ├── publish             --path --ref --tag --force --sign
│   └── update [name]       --all --output -o
├── sys
│   └── create              --name -n(required) --output -o(dir!) --version --force --output-json
└── version
```

---

## Findings

### 1. `--output` / `-o` means two different things (HIGH) ✅ DONE

| Command | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `int create -o` | **destination directory** on disk |
| `sys create -o` | **destination directory** on disk |
| everything else (18 uses) | **output format** (plain/json) |

A user who learns `-o` = format from `skills list -o json` will be surprised when `int create -o foo` writes a directory named `foo`. This is the most dangerous inconsistency because it's silent — no error, just a different effect.

**Fix direction:** rename the directory flag in `int create` and `sys create` to `--dir` / `--out-dir` (keep `-o` reserved for format everywhere). `int create` already has `--output-json` for the machine-readable path, so the format slot is free. Backward-compat: keep `--output` as a hidden deprecated alias for one release.

---

### 2. `--output-json` vs `--output json` — two machine-readable conventions (HIGH) ✅ DONE

| Command | Machine-readable output |
|---|---|
| `int create` | `--output-json <path>` (writes to file, `-` = stdout) |
| `sys create` | `--output-json <path>` (same) |
| `int list`, `int describe`, all `skills`, all `deploy`, all `release` | `--output json` (writes to stdout) |

So `int create` has *both* a `--version` template tag flag and a separate `--output-json` file path, while its sibling `int describe` uses `--output json`. A user scripting across `int describe --output json` and `int create --output-json result.json` has to learn two patterns for the same CLI.

**Fix direction:** converge on `--output json` for stdout everywhere; keep `--output-json <path>` only where a file artifact is genuinely needed (scaffold result documents), but document it as the exception. Alternatively, add `--output json` to `int create`/`sys create` for parity and deprecate `--output-json`.

---

### 3. `--version` means three different things (MEDIUM) ✅ DONE

| Context | `--version` meaning |
|---|---|
| root (`intropy --version`) | CLI version (cobra built-in) |
| `int create`, `int describe`, `deploy init`, `sys create` | **template library release tag** |
| `release create` | **version to publish** (required) |
| `release view` | positional arg, not a flag |
| `deploy <component> [version]` | positional arg, not a flag |

The comment in `deploy_init.go` shows the authors know about this ("Named --version to match int create and int describe... cobra keeps it local to the root rather than persistent, so the name is free here"). But `release create --version 1.2.0` and `int create --version v3` mean entirely different things (a semver you are *publishing* vs a template tag you are *consuming*). And `release view` puts version positional while `release create` puts it in a flag.

**Fix direction:** rename template-tag flags to `--template-version` (or `--template-tag`) in `int create`, `int describe`, `deploy init`, `sys create`. Keep `--version` on `release create` where it genuinely is the release version. This frees `--version` from ambiguity and aligns with the already-existing Go struct field name `templateVersion` in `deploy_init.go`.

---

### 4. Version as positional vs flag (MEDIUM) ✅ DONE (`skills publish --tag` → `--version`; positional/flag alignment of release create/view left as-is by design)

| Command | Version passed as |
|---|---|
| `deploy <component> [version]` | positional (2nd arg) |
| `release view <component> <version>` | positional (2nd arg) |
| `release create <component> --version X` | flag (required) |
| `skills publish --tag X` | flag named `--tag` |
| `int create --version` | flag (template tag) |

`release create` and `release view` are the same domain (release manifests) but disagree. `skills publish --tag` introduces yet another synonym for "version".

**Fix direction:** pick one. Since `release create` needs several other flags anyway, keeping `--version` there is fine, but consider `release create <component> <version>` positional to match `release view`. Rename `skills publish --tag` to `--version` for cross-CLI consistency (the OCI tag *is* the skill version — the code even says "The tag becomes the skill version in the OCI config").

---

### 5. `--name` / `-n` shorthand collision with `--limit -n` (LOW) ✅ DONE (`--limit` is long-only now)

| Command | `-n` shorthand |
|---|---|
| `int create -n` | `--name` (integration name) |
| `sys create -n` | `--name` (system name) |
| `release list -n` | `--limit` (max releases) |

`-n` for `--name` and `-n` for `--limit` are different commands so there's no runtime conflict, but muscle memory across the CLI is misleading. `kubectl` uses `-n` for namespace; `docker` doesn't use `-n` for limit.

**Fix direction:** drop the `-n` shorthand from `release list --limit` (keep `--limit` long-only, or use `-l` if free).

---

### 6. `--env -e` means different things in deploy vs deploy init (LOW) ✅ DONE (`deploy init` now takes `--environments`, plural, no shorthand)

| Command | `--env -e` |
|---|---|
| `deploy`, `deploy diff`, `deploy sync` | **single** target environment (required) |
| `deploy init` | **list** of environments to scaffold overlays for (optional, repeatable) |

Same flag name, same shorthand, different cardinality and optionality. A user typing `deploy init -e staging` expecting "target staging" will instead get "scaffold an overlay for staging among others".

**Fix direction:** rename in `deploy init` to `--envs` or keep `--env` but drop the `-e` shorthand there to force a pause. Better: rename to `--environments` (plural signals list).

---

### 7. `deploy` is both a runnable command and a parent (DESIGN NOTE) ✅ DONE (deploy is now a pure parent; the runnable form is `deploy pin`)

`intropy deploy <component>` works, and `intropy deploy diff|init|promote|status|sync` also works. Cobra resolves subcommand names before positional args, and the Long description even documents this: "The subcommand names win over the component argument, so a component actually called diff, init, promote, status or sync is not reachable this way."

This is a deliberate design choice and documented, but it means a component named `sync` can never be deployed. Compare with `release`, which is purely a parent (`release create/list/view`) — no runnable `release` itself.

**Fix direction:** acceptable if documented (it is), but consider making `deploy` non-runnable and requiring an explicit verb (`deploy pin`?) for symmetry with `release` and `skills`. Low priority — the current design is at least self-aware.

---

### 8. `--from` / `--to` vs `--env` pattern (LOW)

`deploy promote` uses `--from`/`--to` for environments, while every other deploy subcommand uses `--env`. This is actually *good* (promote has two environments, others have one), but the shorthand inconsistency remains: `--env` has `-e` everywhere, while `--from`/`--to` have no shorthands. That's fine — just noting it's intentional.

No fix needed.

---

### 9. `skills collection add` requires flags for what siblings take positionally (LOW)

| Command | Primary identifier |
|---|---|
| `skills collection add` | `--name` + `--ref` (both flags, both required) |
| `skills collection update <alias>` | positional |
| `skills collection publish <spec> <ref>` | positional |

So within the same `collection` group, add takes flags, update takes positional alias, publish takes positional spec+ref. The `add` case is understandable (two pieces of data), but a user might expect `skills collection add <name> <ref>` to work, mirroring `publish <spec> <ref>`.

**Fix direction:** accept `--name`/`--ref` as flags (explicit is fine for registration), but consider also accepting two positional args `skills collection add <name> <ref>` for parity with `publish`. Or leave as-is — this is minor.

---

### 10. `--values -f` type inconsistency: StringArray vs StringSlice (LOW) ✅ DONE (both are StringArray now)

| Command | Flag type |
|---|---|
| `int create` | `StringArrayVarP` (no comma splitting) |
| `deploy init` | `StringSliceVarP` (comma splitting enabled) |

pflag's `StringSlice` splits on commas (`-f a,b` = two files); `StringArray` does not. Same flag name, same shorthand, different splitting behavior. A user who writes `--values base.yaml,extra.yaml` under `deploy init` gets two files; under `int create` they get one file literally named `base.yaml,extra.yaml`.

**Fix direction:** pick one — `StringArray` is the safer default (file paths can contain commas). Change `deploy init` to `StringArrayVarP`.

---

## Summary of recommended changes (priority order)

| # | Change | Commands affected | Breaking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rename directory flag `--output`→`--out-dir` | `int create`, `sys create` | Yes (deprecate old) |
| 2 | Converge machine-readable on `--output json` | `int create`, `sys create` | Additive |
| 3 | Rename template tag `--version`→`--template-version` | `int create`, `int describe`, `deploy init`, `sys create` | Yes (deprecate old) |
| 4 | Align `skills publish --tag`→`--version` | `skills publish` | Yes (deprecate old) |
| 5 | Drop `-n` from `release list --limit` | `release list` | Minor |
| 6 | Rename `deploy init --env`→`--environments` | `deploy init` | Yes (deprecate old) |
| 7 | Unify `--values` to StringArray | `deploy init` | Edge-case behavior |
| 8 | (Optional) positional args for `collection add` | `skills collection add` | Additive |

Items 1–3 are the high-value fixes: they remove genuine ambiguity where the same flag name silently does different things. Items 4–7 are polish. Item 8 is optional.

## Workstream 1 — Agent/human writing guidance (do first, so everything else follows it)

### 1.1 Create `AGENTS.md` at repo root

New file. Sections:

- **Scope** — applies to all Go source in this repo; covers code comments, cobra help text, and user-facing output/error strings.
- **Code comments** —
  - Explain *why* and *what invariant holds*, not *what changed*. Never reference PRs, fixes, "used to", "now", "previously".
  - Doc comment on every exported symbol (golint convention).
  - Prefer ≤ 10 lines per doc block. If you need more, the extra content probably belongs in `docs/`.
  - "Deliberately not X" comments are encouraged when they prevent a plausible wrong refactor (see `internal/gitops/remote.go` for the exemplar).
  - No TODO/FIXME/HACK in committed code — file an issue instead.
- **Help text** —
  - `Short:` one line, imperative verb, no period. ("Pin a component's image digest into an environment")
  - `Long:` what it does, what it costs, what flags change the behavior. Target ≤ 150 words; hard ceiling ~200. Architecture rationale and philosophy belong in `docs/`, not `--help`.
  - `Use:` positional args in `<>`, optional in `[]`, variadic as `name...`.
- **Flag descriptions** — use the shared constants in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` (created in 3.1). Never hand-write a new description for `--output`, `--env`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--domain`, `--system`, `--template-version`.
- **Runtime output** —
  - Progress/status: lowercase, present tense, no trailing period, to stderr. ("syncing api on argocd.example.com at a1b2c3d")
  - Completion: same voice, to stderr for plain output.
  - Errors: front-load what failed, then the remediation on a second line if there is one. No editorializing ("un-deploying what they run" — cut).
  - Machine-readable output goes to stdout; everything human goes to stderr. Never mix.
- **Vocabulary** — "image digest" not "bits"; "environment" not "env" in prose; `->` for transitions, `@` for version pins, and don't mix them in one message.

One line: `See AGENTS.md.` (Single source of truth; CLAUDE.md is a pointer so the two never drift. This matches the convention in repos that support both agents.)

### 1.3 Link from `CONTRIBUTING.md`

Add a "Writing style" subsection under **Code Standards**, two sentences, pointing to `AGENTS.md`. Also add a PR-checklist item: "Help text, output text, and comments follow `AGENTS.md`."

# Writing style — comments, help text, and CLI output

This file is the house style for everything a reader sees: Go doc comments,
`--help` output, and the strings a command prints or returns as errors. It
applies to every Go file in this repository. Keep it short enough that it can
be re-read before every PR.

---

## Code comments

**Explain why, not what changed.** A comment answers the question the code
cannot: the invariant, the trade-off, the reason a non-obvious choice is the
safe one. It never narrates history.

- Never reference a PR, issue, fix, or the past tense of the code itself.
  "Used to", "now", "previously", "after the refactor", "fixes #123" are all
  forbidden. Git history already knows; the reader of the code does not care.
- A doc comment on every exported symbol. One or two sentences is usually
  enough. `golint` enforces this; don't make a reviewer do it.
- Target ≤ 10 lines per doc block. If you need more, the extra content
  belongs in `docs/` or a README, not above the function.
- "Deliberately not X" comments are encouraged when they stop a plausible
  wrong refactor. `internal/gitops/remote.go` is the exemplar: it says the
  function is *not* used to derive the cache directory, and why.
- No TODO, FIXME, HACK, or XXX in committed code. File an issue instead.

---

## Help text (cobra)

`--help` is reference material, not a blog post. A reader in a terminal wants
to know what the command does, what it costs, and which flags change the
behavior. Philosophy and motivation belong in `docs/`.

- **`Short:`** one line, imperative verb, no trailing period.
  Good: `Pin a component's image digest into an environment`
  Bad:  `This command pins the image digest.`
- **`Long:`** target ≤ 150 words, hard ceiling ~200. Cover: what it does,
  what it reads, what it writes, what can go wrong that the user can prevent.
  Cut: why the command exists, why GitOps is good, architecture essays.
- **`Use:`** positional args in `<>`, optional in `[]`, variadic as `name...`.
  Good: `pin <component> [version]`
  Bad:  `pin COMPONENT [VERSION]`, `pin <component> [<version>]`

If a `Long:` draft exceeds 200 words, the excess is almost always the second
paragraph onwards. Move it to a file under `docs/` and keep the help text
to usage.

---

## Flag descriptions

Use the shared constants in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`. Never hand-write a new
description for a flag another command already has:

- `--output`, `--env`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--domain`,
  `--system`, `--template-version` all have constants.
- If you add a flag that several commands will share, add a constant first.
- Flag descriptions are fragments, not sentences: no trailing period, no
  "This flag…". Start with the noun. Good: `target environment (required)`.

---

## Runtime output

A CLI's output is read twice: once by a human scanning, once by a script
parsing. The two never share a stream.

- **stdout is for results.** Tables, JSON, the thing the command was run to
  produce.
- **stderr is for everything else.** Progress, warnings, completion messages,
  errors. A pipeline reading stdout must never see a status line.

### Voice

- Progress and completion: **lowercase, present tense, no trailing period**.
  Good: `syncing api on argocd.example.com at a1b2c3d`
  Good: `published ghcr.io/example/skills/pr-review:1.2.0`
  Bad:  `Published ghcr.io/…`  `Sync complete.`
- Empty states follow the same rule: `no skills installed`, not
  `No skills installed.`
- A follow-up hint naming a command goes on its own line, in backticks:
  `use 'intropy skills add <ref>' to add one`

### Errors

- Front-load what failed. The remediation, if there is one, goes on a second
  line. Do not editorialize — the user is already reading an error.
  Good: `pending change is a1b2c3d, not the f4e5d6c you reviewed`
        `run 'intropy deploy diff api --env staging' before syncing`
  Bad:  `…has advanced since you reviewed it — you really should read the new diff…`
- Wrap errors with context as they travel up: `fmt.Errorf("pull %s: %w", …)`.
  The outermost prefix names the command or operation, not the internals.

### Vocabulary

- **image digest**, not "bits", "artifacts", or "the images".
- **environment** in prose, `--env` only when naming the flag.
- `->` for a transition (`1.0 -> 1.1`), ` @ ` for a pin (`api @ 1.2.0`).
  Never mix the two in one message.
- A commit SHA is shown short (7 chars) unless the full value is the point.

---

## What this file is not

It does not replace `CONTRIBUTING.md` (workflow, tests, commit convention) or
`README.md` (what the CLI is). When those disagree with this file, this file
wins on writing style and loses on everything else.

# Why `deploy init` exists and how it lays out a system

Onboarding a component by hand is entirely manual: somebody hand-writes
`component.yaml`, a `base/` and an overlay per environment, for every block,
in every customer repository. `deploy init` does that work, filling in every
fact the CLI can derive — the block's workload, the app-ids that belong in a
Dapr component's `scopes`, the environments `deploy.yaml` defines, the
registry.

## Placeholders, not guesses

Complete manifests are not the goal. Connection strings, hosts, credentials
and cron schedules cannot be derived, so they are emitted as
`REPLACE-ME-<HINT>` placeholders and reported as a list when the run
finishes. Filling those in is the developer's remaining job. Image tags are
deliberately not in that list: `intropy deploy` pins digests, and scaffolding
must never pin one.

## The `host` directory and Dapr ownership

A system's shared objects — the Dapr pub/sub and secret store its blocks
resolve by name, and the secrets behind them — go in a `host` directory of
their own. A Dapr Component is namespace-scoped and every integration in the
namespace shares it, so exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one; the
host directory is what gives them that owner, and `scopes:` is what limits
who may use them.

## Git strategy

Nothing is pushed to the default branch: a tree full of placeholders would be
picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. The run pushes
`deploy-init/<domain>-<system>` for review instead. Re-running is additive
and safe — a file that already exists and differs is reported and left alone
unless `--force` is given, and `--force` still refuses to overwrite an
overlay that pins a digest.
